text:
Nine games without a win (0-8-1), outscored 37-18, and on Saturday a third-period lead against Columbus that turned into another loss and "Fire Hiller" chants from the crowd. Auston Matthews called it "inexcusable" and said "We should be embarrassed," as Daily Faceoff reported. Jim Hiller, hired in the summer to replace Craig Berube, got a vote of confidence from general manager John Chayka after an 0-6 homestand last week. The skid has kept going since.

This isn't bad luck. The Leafs had 44% of the expected goals in the streak (expected goals measure the quality of chances) and 46% on the season, both overall and at 5v5. At 8-14-3 they do have about four or five points fewer than their play has earned, and Sergei Bobrovsky's last five starts are a big part of it: .827, 7.6 goals worse than expected, 0-5-0. But even a fair record would be a middling one. Our playoff odds are 2%.

The noise around the team is getting louder. Matthews is the subject of trade columns, reports describe the Leafs as walking on eggshells around William Nylander, and the handling of rookie Gavin McKenna, benched at times by Hiller this season, has become its own debate.

The one line that works is Matthews with Jack Roslovic and Easton Cowan: 11 goals for and 4 against at 5v5. Jake McCabe and Darren Raddysh, the top pair, get only 44% of the expected goals. Morgan Rielly is back in the lineup.
